stories.notes: Empty acceptance criteria on a complex cross-platform live preview feature spanning GO, UP, and MX. Openspec must elaborate AC with technical depth (preview rendering pipeline, real-time sync, multi-platform content projection) before speckit hardens testability, security (preview token validation, content injection), and edge cases (concurrent edits, stale previews, platform-specific rendering divergence).

agentContributions.notes: Novel story — live preview capability does not exist yet. Acceptance criteria were empty, so all verification criteria are derived from the description. VCs explicitly cover both named behaviours: real-time preview rendering and no-publish-cycle operation. Contentstack is unreachable at test time, so VCs assume a mocked Contentstack client and verify what our code renders given known responses.

Openspec provided empty acceptance criteria, so all 13 criteria are new. Derived entirely from the story title '[GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS' which implies real-time preview rendering without a publish cycle across three locales. AC-1/AC-2 cover the two core named behaviours (real-time update, no-publish-cycle). AC-3 covers the three locales. AC-4/AC-5 cover connection loss and recovery. AC-6 covers unsupported content types. AC-7 covers empty/null content. AC-8 covers malformed responses. AC-9 covers timeouts. AC-10 covers authentication/authorization. AC-11 covers accessibility. AC-12 covers concurrent editing. AC-13 covers navigation resilience. The original story description is extremely thin (title repeated as description with no detail), which is flagged for human attention. No source files were available for review; criteria may need refinement once implementation context is known.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents derived all 13 acceptance criteria from the title alone since the original ACs were empty and the description was extremely thin. Speckit's contribution largely restates openspec's work rather than adding a distinct hardening layer — both describe the same 13 criteria with no evidence of iterative refinement. Critical metadata contradiction: acceptanceChanged is false on both agents despite claiming 13 new criteria were created, and the story's acceptanceCriteria array remains empty [], suggesting criteria were not persisted or the pipeline failed to write back. A cross-platform feature spanning GO, UP, and MX with concurrent editing, connection loss, accessibility, and authentication concerns likely warranted at least one story split, yet splitCount is 0 for both agents. All criteria are speculative given the thin source material. Human review required to validate criteria, confirm persistence, and assess whether a split is needed.
